dedupe_keys.name: permanent gnss reference station network of morocco ancfcc

description: The Moroccan national land registry, cadastre and mapping agency, ANCFCC, describes its network of permanent GNSS reference stations on its cartography pages, alongside the planimetric geodetic network, the levelling network and the geoid. The page says the network is made up of eighteen permanent stations and lists them in Tangier, Al Hoceima, Oujda, Rabat, Casablanca, Fès, Guercif, El Jadida, Essaouira, Marrakech, Beni Mellal, Errachidia, Agadir, Ouarzazate, Guelmim, Laâyoune and Dakhla; each station is a geodetic point on a clear site, usually a rooftop, whose antenna tracks GNSS satellites above 5 degrees of elevation. Two kinds of observations are made available to users: daily observations at a 30-second rate and hourly observations at a 1-second rate, both as compressed RINEX files. A densification project planned 12 more stations for 2017. No licence is stated and prices are not given on the page read; requests go through the agency's contacts. Caveats: the page names seventeen cities for eighteen stations, the densification status after 2017 is not stated, and the page is in French. Coverage is Morocco. It supports positioning infrastructure studies, crustal deformation monitoring for earthquake hazard, and space weather effects on GNSS; related records are SLCORSnet of Sri Lanka and TUSAGA-Aktif of Türkiye.
